title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Alternative Methods - Single Source
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A municipality decides to buy all its future police radios from Motorola, even though Harris and Kenwood make similar radios, in order to ensure seamless compatibility and reduce training costs. This is an example of a:
questions.explain: A single source procurement occurs when multiple viable suppliers exist, but the agency intentionally chooses one specific vendor for reasons such as standardization, compatibility, or maintenance efficiency. It requires strict legal justification.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Standardization is often used as a justification for which non-competitive sourcing strategy?
questions.explain: Standardizing on a specific manufacturer's equipment to reduce training time or ensure inter-operability is a common rationale for approving a Single Source procurement.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When writing a justification for a Single Source procurement, a buyer should emphasize:
options: Why competition is impossible due to patent laws
The immediate threat to public safety
The strategic, financial, or operational benefits of standardizing on one vendor despite the existence of other market players
The vendor's willingness to skip negotiations
questions.explain: Single source justifications must defend the decision to intentionally bypass available competition, usually by citing long-term savings from standardization, compatibility constraints, or specific administrative efficiencies.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A valid difference between a Sole Source and a Single Source is:
options: Sole Source refers to construction; Single Source refers to services
Sole Source means no other supplier exists; Single Source means the agency is voluntarily restricting competition to one vendor for strategic reasons
There is no difference; the terms are perfectly synonymous
questions.explain: A sole source is driven by market reality (only one exists). A single source is an agency choice to waive competition and use one supplier among many, typically for standardization.
